v.rationale:
All three suites pass: impl-1 18 tests, impl-2 15, impl-3 20. Probes covered malformed rate items, scalar rate lists, 429/403/400, whitespace and unicode-digit postcodes, whether 5xx exhaustion is reported, and a non-JSON 200. Each probe file was deleted afterwards. All three stay within the 5s budget and correctly avoid retrying 401 and 404.

impl-2 has the most serious bug: when the carrier returns a rate item missing a key, it responds with a 500 instead of the fallback, which breaks checkout's guarantee of an answer. It also reports every fallback, including ordinary 5xx exhaustion, which floods alerting. It hand-rolls the retry loop rather than using Http::retry and validates inline. It ranks last.

impl-1 and impl-3 share one gap: neither checks the shape of individual rate items. impl-3's error mapping is slightly richer (it retries 429 and reports unexpected 4xx such as 403, which impl-1 silently swallows). Its test hygiene is weaker, though: unused imports in Pest.php, real sleeps because Sleep::fake() is never called, an unrequested throttle middleware, a tautological ShouldntReport test, and manual reportable() hooks.

impl-1 is the simplest and most idiomatic. It uses Http::retry with an isTransient predicate, a `never` handleFailure, Exceptions::fake with assertReported/assertNothingReported, and preventStrayRequests set globally. That makes it first, with impl-3 second and impl-2 third.
